subject: Discovery: sample query pack + redaction rubric for LegalTech pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Myers <sarah@legaltech.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery: sample query pack + redaction rubric for LegalTech pilot

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and a small ask so we can scope the model-fit work on our side.

Recap of needs (what I heard):
- Contract summarization with clause-level extraction and change-tracking.
- Clause classification (assignment to ~25 label classes you showed).
- Redaction / PII handling for downstream sharing and auditability.
- High precision on legal entity and dates; tolerant recall for metadata.

What we’ll do immediately:
- Run a lightweight model-fit smoke test across two candidate families (small/medium) to validate latency and a basic accuracy baseline.
- Provide a prompt-set-driven evaluation (50–100 seeded prompts per intent) and surface regression risks.

Request: could you share a representative sample pack of customer queries and edge cases? Specifically:
- ~200–300 real customer queries (anonymized is fine) across the main workflows (summarization, clause search, classification).
- 15–25 edge cases where the model historically failed (examples of false positives/negatives).
- Mark any examples that must be fully redacted before transfer (PII/highly sensitive).

I attached a one-tab template (example_query_template.xlsx) with the format that helps our evaluation pipeline (columns: id, intent, original_text, redaction_level, expected_label). If you can return CSV/XLSX, that’s ideal.

Redaction guidance from our side (starting point):
- Level 0: keep full text (non-sensitive).
- Level 1: redact direct identifiers (names, emails, phone numbers) but keep contextual tokens (company names, dates).
- Level 2: strip and mask whole paragraphs for high-sensitivity items (SSNs, financial account numbers).

If you prefer, we can accept pre-redacted samples and a small unredacted subset under an NDA to help quantify drop in model accuracy. No blocker either way — we’ll work with what you can share.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Once we have the pack, expect an initial smoke report in 3 business days (token-latency + labeled precision/recall on core intents).
- Follow-ups: sample-driven prompt set recommendations + suggested quantization/profile for Dedicated or Private.

Next steps: please send the pack and name the person on your side who will own the upload (S3/Drive). We’ll use the redaction rubric above unless you specify otherwise.

Thanks — looking forward to the examples.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: example_query_template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 tab)

From: Sarah Myers <sarah@legaltech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery: sample query pack + redaction rubric for LegalTech pilot

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear summary and the template. We pulled together a first tranche and attached it (legaltech_sample_queries_v1.csv). A few notes:

- File contains ~120 customer queries covering summarization and clause search; we’ll follow up with more classification examples next week to hit your 200–300 target.
- I flagged 8 rows as Level 2 (full mask) where contracts include client SSNs or account numbers.
- Edge cases: included 12 examples that broke our prior heuristic rules.

Question: for items flagged Level 2, would you prefer token-level masking (e.g., [REDACTED-SSN]) or full paragraph removal? We don’t want to accidentally remove context that matters for classification.

We can upload the full set to a shared S3 bucket (I can grant a temporary presigned URL). Who should I grant access to?

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Product 
LegalTech, Inc.
sarah@legaltech.com

Attachment: legaltech_sample_queries_v1.csv (CSV, 120 rows)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Myers <sarah@legaltech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery: sample query pack + redaction rubric for LegalTech pilot

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the quick turnaround and the first tranche. I’ve looped in Ben (solutions lead for legal vertical) and Irene (inference engineer) so we can coordinate the smoke tests.

Quick answers:
- For Level 2 examples we recommend token-level masking that preserves sentence structure (e.g., "The client SSN is [REDACTED-SSN]") rather than deleting paragraphs. That keeps useful context for classification while removing the sensitive token.
- Access: a presigned S3 link to an internal folder is perfect; please add access for ben_carter@redwood.ai and irene_choi@redwood.ai. If you need our AWS account id let me know.

What we’ll run on arrival:
- Baseline smoke tests against two model candidates:
  • Llama2-13b-chat (instruction-tuned) — higher throughput, lower memory footprint.
  • Falcon-40B-instruct quantized (Q8/Q4 testing path) — better language understanding in some long-clause cases.

We’ll annotate per-example failure modes (false positive clause extractions, mislabeling) and surface items that are likely to trigger quality regressions under quantization. We’ll also include an early suggestion for prompt templates and a short sensitivity rubric.

I attached a short redaction_rubric_v1.pdf that matches the token-level examples — please confirm and we’ll proceed. Expect the first smoke report by end of day Thursday.

Best,
Hannah

Attachment: redaction_rubric_v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Myers <sarah@legaltech.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery: sample query pack + redaction rubric for LegalTech pilot

Hi Sarah — Ben here. Quick operational notes and a small checklist so we don’t miss anything for the evaluation:

Checklist for the pack upload:
- Folder: presigned S3 to include files and a small README (format, column definitions).
- Examples: aim for at least 250 rows total across intents for a robust signal; if you can include label golds for a 100-row subset that helps our precision/recall numbers.
- Edge-case labeling: add a short "why this failed" note for each edge-case row if possible.

Model & evaluation notes:
- We’ll run a small prompt-ensemble: two prompt templates per intent to test sensitivity to few-shot examples.
- Metrics we’ll surface: per-intent precision/recall, top-1 label accuracy, latency p50/p95 on both hosted vs. dedicated config.
- If you have SLO targets (e.g., 95% precision for clause detection), include them in the README so we can prioritize tuning recommendations.

Logistics:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4567890 (I updated the deal stage to "Pilot - sample pack received").
- Eval deck (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/eval-deck-legaltech-2026 — we’ll upload the smoke report there and share a short recording.

We’ll aim for the smoke results and recommended prompt set tomorrow EOD. If anything changes on your side with more examples or a different redaction approach, ping me and we’ll adapt.

Meeting?: Hannah and I can do a 30-min follow-up on Thursday to walk through the smoke report — I placed a tentative slot on the calendar for 12/23 if that works.

Thanks — looking forward to the samples.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Legal Verticals | Redwood Inference
